anti_patterns: Acting on unfinalized optimistic outputs before the challenge window closes
Accepting inference from a modelId whose commitment was updated or deprecated without re-pinning
Treating a validity proof as a correctness proof of the model itself (it proves faithful execution, not that the model is good)
Running non-deterministic floating-point builds through the fraud-proof path so submitter and challenger diverge on identical inputs
Blocking the agent loop synchronously on proving or challenge windows instead of suspending and resuming on settlement
avoid_when: Latency-sensitive tasks where challenge windows or proving times exceed the decision deadline
Cost-sensitive workloads where proof verification gas outweighs the value of trust
Low-stakes outputs where a plain offchain call plus a retry policy is sufficient
benefits: Trustless inference: agent and counterparties verify the result without trusting any single server
Deterministic settlement: verified outputs (InferenceVerified events, finalized opML claims) are auditable and replayable
Model and input privacy options via zero-knowledge submodels while keeping correctness guarantees
Composable primitive: registry modelIds and verifier interfaces (ERC-7992 style) let agents switch models without reintegration
best_practices: Pin the exact modelId plus commitment hashes in the agent's policy, and re-resolve them before each high-value action
Embed a nonce or salt in every input commitment to prevent replay of single-use inferences
Suspend the agent task on settlement wait with an explicit deadline, then retry, switch models, or escalate to a human
Log proof blobs, commitments, and settlement transaction hashes alongside the agent trace for audit
Partition models so only privacy-sensitive submodels pay zkML proving costs and bulk compute runs optimistically
context: Agents whose state-changing actions (transfers, votes, trades, access grants) must rest on model inference that counterparties can verify: heavy inference runs offchain, but correctness is settled onchain — either by a zero-knowledge proof checked by a verifier contract against a registered model commitment (zkML, e.g. ERC-7992 verifyInference), or by optimistic submission plus a challenge window with bisection and single-step FPVM arbitration (opML). The agent requests inference, waits for settlement, and acts only on verified or finalized outputs.
design_principles: Never act on unsettled inference for state-changing operations
Separate execution (offchain, fast) from verification (onchain, minimal)
Pin model identity before trusting any output
Make settlement waits explicit, bounded, and resumable
name: onchain-ai-inference
references: Ethereum ERC Editors, Verifiable ML Model Inference (ZKML) ERC-7992 — https://ercs.ethereum.org/ERCS/erc-7992
Conway et al., opML: Optimistic Machine Learning on Blockchain, 2024 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.17555
OPML Labs, OPML: Optimistic Machine Learning on Blockchain — https://github.com/OPML-Labs/opml
technology_stack: Solidity verifier and registry contracts (ERC-7992 style)
Agent orchestration with async settlement waits
tradeoffs: Proving latency (zkML) or challenge-window delay (opML) before outputs become actionable
Proof generation and onchain verification gas costs, steep for large models
Deterministic quantized builds required, constraining model choice and framework freedom
Optimistic path relies on cryptoeconomic AnyTrust assumptions and watcher liveness, not pure cryptography
use_cases: DeFi agent executing trades on verified risk-model scores
DAO governance agent acting on settled proposal-analysis outputs
Insurance agent settling claims on verifiable damage-assessment inference
Prediction-market agent resolving markets on proven model outputs
